html:
The Duchy of Courland and Semigallia was a German-ruled duchy in western Latvia from 1561 to 1795, a vassal of Poland-Lithuania.

It was made from the ruins of the Livonian Order in the Livonian War. Under Duke Jacob Kettler, from 1642 to 1682, it built a merchant fleet, ironworks and shipyards. Jacob even founded colonies on Tobago in the Caribbean and on an island in the Gambia River in Africa, one of the smallest states ever to try.

The colonies were lost within decades, and the duchy suffered in the wars between Sweden and Poland. In 1795 it was annexed by the Russian Empire. Its German nobles kept their estates until 1920. The palace of Rundāle, built for its dukes, survives in Latvia.
sum: The Duchy of Courland and Semigallia was a German-ruled duchy in western Latvia from 1561 to 1795, a vassal of Poland-Lithuania.
